parameters.content:
## Trellis Carousel — v1.3

Generates a 3-7 slide social carousel: one plan (Gemini), then one on-brand image per slide (Nano Banana), all sharing an identical style block. Every slide image is generated completely clean of text — the Trellis app composites each slide's title/text afterward in the real brand font (`branches.font_family`) using the brand's actual hex colours.

**In:** POST /webhook/trellis-carousel-generate
```
{ job_id, branch, topic, slide_count,
  target_segment, platform,
  aspect_ratio, style_notes,
  revision_of?, revision_notes? }
```
`slide_count` is clamped to 3-7.
`revision_of` (optional): UUID of a prior job being regenerated. `revision_notes` (optional): free-text feedback on why the prior attempt was rejected - it is appended to the plan prompt and to every slide's image prompt. The app resubmits the SAME original body plus these two fields; the job row's `request_payload` (saved by Upsert Job Record) is what makes that replay possible.

**Out:** job row -> status `awaiting_approval`, with `media_urls` (N items, in slide order), `frame_url` (= slide 1), `caption`, `script` (the full slide plan JSON) set. None of the images have AI-drawn text on them.

Approval + publish happen in the Trellis app (Video Ad Lab), which hands off to the existing B3 social publisher webhook (`trellis-social-publish`) with `media_type: 'carousel'` and `media_urls`.

### v1.3: photography-brief prompts + aspect-aware clean area
Same spirit as the static-ad workflow: slide `title`/`body` are composited by the app afterward, so each slide's `image_prompt` from Gemini is now instructed (in **Prepare Slide Plan**'s `plan_prompt`) to be a pure photography brief - subject, action, setting and mood only, describing what the camera sees and never mentioning text, titles or logos. Visual consistency across slides still does not depend on the model obeying: the shared `style_block`, computed once in code and appended verbatim to every slide's `image_prompt` in **Parse Slide Plan**, now carries real photographic craft language (full-frame camera, 35mm f/2.0, shallow depth of field, natural light, film grain), the real brand hex colours, an aspect-aware clean-area rule (lower quarter for 9:16, lower third for 4:5/1:1/other) reserved for the per-slide text, and a negative clause that now also names common AI failure modes (distorted hands/faces, extra fingers, oversaturation, plastic skin, stock-photo staging, collage/borders/UI) alongside the existing no-text rule.

### v1.2: real brand colours + clean imagery
Brand colours were never reaching the model — `brand_profiles.brand_colors` is `[]` for every brand, so prompts fell back to generic "Colour palette consistent with X" phrasing. **Lookup Branch Style** (new node, reuses the same Supabase credential — no new setup) now reads `branches` directly for `primary_color` / `secondary_color` / `accent_color` (and `font_family`), matching on `branches.slug = body.branch` — a clean equality match against the bare slug the app already sends, unlike `Lookup Brand Profile`'s prefix hack against `brand_profiles.branch`. `Prepare Slide Plan` reads it defensively and bakes `primary`/`secondary`/`accent` straight into the `style_block` it computes once and appends to every slide.
Separately, this workflow no longer asks Gemini to render any text onto slide images — not even the on-slide title. `style_block` now reserves generous negative space (lower third) for text and carries a hard "no text of any kind" negative clause on every slide. The app is responsible for compositing each slide's real title/text, in the real brand font and colours, after generation.

### Setup
1. Credentials — reuse the same 3 as Trellis-Video-Ad-Frame-v1 (Lookup Branch Style reuses the Supabase one, no new credential needed):
   • **Sproutify Trellis** (Supabase) — id `IkIpi5m4OmJ9DvBS`
   • **Gemini API** (Query Auth) — replace `REPLACE_GEMINI_CRED`
   • **Supabase Storage (legacy eyJ service role)** (Header Auth) — replace `REPLACE_SUPABASE_STORAGE_CRED`
2. Prerequisite SQL (Hub, run once — idempotent):
```sql
ALTER TABLE video_ad_jobs ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS format TEXT;
ALTER TABLE video_ad_jobs ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS media_urls JSONB DEFAULT '[]';
ALTER TABLE video_ad_jobs ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS caption TEXT;
ALTER TABLE video_ad_jobs ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS request_payload JSONB;
ALTER TABLE video_ad_jobs ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS revision_of UUID;
ALTER TABLE video_ad_jobs ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS revision_notes TEXT;
```
(`request_payload` / `revision_of` / `revision_notes` are already applied to the live Hub DB - this SQL is for the record / fresh environments.)
3. Activate, then point the Video Ad Lab's carousel action at `https://n8n.sproutify.app/webhook/trellis-carousel-generate`.

This workflow STOPS at `awaiting_approval`. It does not publish anything.

### Why the slides can't drift
Asking Gemini nicely for a 'consistent style' across N separate image generations is not reliable enough on its own. **Prepare Slide Plan** computes ONE `style_block` string in code - including real photographic craft language, the real brand hex colours from `Lookup Branch Style`, the aspect-aware negative-space rule, and the hard no-text/no-artefact rule - and **Parse Slide Plan** appends it VERBATIM to every slide's `image_prompt` after parsing. Consistency (and the absence of on-image text) is guaranteed by the code, not by model compliance. The model is only asked for a pure photography brief per slide (subject/action/setting/mood) - the craft, palette, composition and negative rules always come from the shared block.

### No loop node needed
**Split Slides** fans one plan out into N items; **Generate Slide Image -> Extract Slide Image -> Upload Slide to Storage** then process one item per slide automatically (n8n's default per-item behaviour for regular nodes) - the exact same shape as B3's carousel-child chain (`Prepare Carousel Items -> Create Carousel Child -> Collect Carousel Children`). **Aggregate Slide URLs** re-sorts by `slide_index` and throws if any slide is missing, mirroring B3's `children.length !== source.media_urls.length` check.

### No Vision QA loop here
Unlike the static-ad workflow, carousel slides are not re-checked for on-image text or clean-area clutter after generation - there is no per-slide QA/retry step. The no-text and clean-area rules live entirely in the code-built `style_block`, applied identically to every slide before generation.

nodes.name: Upsert Job Record
nodes.notes: Insert on first run. On a resubmit the row already exists and this 409s harmlessly - onError lets it pass through, mirrors Trellis-Video-Ad-Frame-v1. request_payload persists the exact inbound body (via JSON.stringify) so the app's 'Regenerate' button can replay it unchanged with revision_of/revision_notes added on top. Like media_urls elsewhere in this workflow, confirm on first run that Supabase writes it as real jsonb and not a double-encoded string - documented fallback is a raw HTTP PATCH node with Content-Type: application/json instead of this Supabase node field. CONFIRMED on live runs: PostgREST stores this JSON.stringify'd value as a jsonb *string*, not a native array/object (jsonb_typeof = 'string'). The app normalizes it on read via parseJsonbField() in services/videoAdService.ts. Do NOT remove the JSON.stringify without updating that normalizer - and note jsonb_array_length / the GIN index cannot be used while it is stored this way.

nodes.name: Lookup Brand Profile
nodes.notes: OPTIONAL supplement only (pronunciation_guide, default_setting). Name, tone and colours now come from `Lookup Branch Style` (the `branches` table), which is keyed by the exact slug the app sends. brand_profiles is keyed by DOMAIN, so this prefix match misses e.g. slug 'rejoice' vs 'letsrejoice.app' - that is expected and harmless now, since nothing essential depends on it.

nodes.name: Lookup Branch Style
nodes.notes: Exact slug match against branches.slug - the app sends the bare slug (e.g. atlurbanfarms), which matches this column exactly, unlike Lookup Brand Profile's prefix hack against brand_profiles.branch. Supplies primary_color / secondary_color / accent_color (and font_family) for the real brand colours; brand_profiles.brand_colors is empty for every brand, so this is the only source of truth for hex values used in image prompts.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ contents: [{ parts: [{ text: $('Prepare Slide Plan').item.json.plan_prompt }] }], generationConfig: { temperature: 0.8, maxOutputTokens: 4096, responseMimeType: 'application/json', responseSchema: { type: 'OBJECT', properties: { caption: { type: 'STRING' }, slides: { type: 'ARRAY', items: { type: 'OBJECT', properties: { title: { type: 'STRING' }, body: { type: 'STRING' }, image_prompt: { type: 'STRING' } }, required: ['title','body','image_prompt'] } } }, required: ['caption','slides'] } } }) }}

nodes.name: Generate Slide Plan
nodes.notes: Schema-enforced JSON (responseMimeType + responseSchema) so the slide plan is always parseable. maxOutputTokens is large because N slide prompts plus thinking tokens add up, and truncation makes the whole plan unparseable.

nodes.name: Parse Slide Plan
nodes.notes: Defensive JSON parse (raw parse -> regex-extracted {...} block -> 1-slide fallback). Appends the identical style_block to every slide.image_prompt so slide-to-slide consistency does not depend on the model - as of v1.3 that block is a real photography brief (full-frame camera / lens / aperture / lighting language), the real brand hex colours, an aspect-aware clean-area rule (lower quarter for 9:16, lower third otherwise) and a negative clause covering both on-image text and common AI rendering flaws. The workflow no longer asks Gemini to render any on-slide text (not even the title); the Trellis app composites it afterward in the real brand font. Per-slide image_prompt values from the model are meant to be pure photography briefs (subject/action/setting/mood only) per the plan_prompt instructions in Prepare Slide Plan.

nodes.name: Split Slides
nodes.notes: One output item per slide, in order. Everything downstream (Generate Slide Image / Extract Slide Image / Upload Slide to Storage) processes these N items automatically - no splitInBatches loop needed, same shape as B3's carousel-child chain.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ contents: [{ parts: [{ text: $json.image_prompt }] }], generationConfig: { responseModalities: ['IMAGE'], imageConfig: { aspectRatio: $json.aspect_ratio } } }) }}

nodes.name: Generate Slide Image
nodes.notes: Nano Banana 2 (gemini-3.1-flash-image), one call per input item (per slide). Runs sequentially in n8n's default execution order.

nodes.name: Extract Slide Image
nodes.notes: runOnceForEachItem, same idiom as E5's 'Audio base64 to Binary' node - $('Split Slides').item correctly resolves to the paired slide for whichever item is currently executing.

nodes.name: Upload Slide to Storage
nodes.notes: Same episode-assets bucket as Trellis-Video-Ad-Frame-v1, under a static-ads/ prefix. MUST use the legacy eyJ... JWT service role key - upsert:false + a randomised filename avoids the UPDATE RLS policy on Storage, same as Frame v1. Runs once per slide.

nodes.name: Aggregate Slide URLs
nodes.notes: Mirrors B3's 'Collect Carousel Children' validation: throws if the item count reaching this node does not match the planned slide count (a slide that hit its error branch never arrives here), then re-sorts by slide_index so order is guaranteed regardless of async completion order.

nodes.name: Update: Awaiting Approval
nodes.notes: Terminal state for this workflow. media_urls is written as a JSON.stringify'd array via the Supabase node - after first run, confirm in the table editor that the column stores a real JSON array and not a double-encoded string; if PostgREST stores it as a scalar string, switch this field to a raw HTTP PATCH node with Content-Type: application/json instead. CONFIRMED on live runs: PostgREST stores this JSON.stringify'd value as a jsonb *string*, not a native array/object (jsonb_typeof = 'string'). The app normalizes it on read via parseJsonbField() in services/videoAdService.ts. Do NOT remove the JSON.stringify without updating that normalizer - and note jsonb_array_length / the GIN index cannot be used while it is stored this way.
